summary: Sudden server-error surge: accept-queue handoff + KV-prefetch thrash causing elevated 5xx in prod-us-west
description: Issue summary: At ~2026-03-12 10:18 PDT customers started observing elevated 5xx responses on several chat and embedding endpoints. Impact: multiple enterprise tenants (notably Finlytics Analytics) experienced request failures and increased tail latency; visible error rate rose from ~0.2% baseline to ~8% over a 15 minute window, with streaming sessions dropping. Environment: prod-us-west (us-west-2), mixed workload: long chat sessions + bulk embedding uploads. Steps to reproduce: 1) Run mixed workload: concurrent long-chat sessions (seq len > 4k) with an embedding bulk upload (100k vectors) from same tenant. 2) Observe apigw request queue growth and progressive 502/503 responses. Logs / metrics: api-gateway accept_queue_depth spiked to 18k, apigw 5xx rate climbed to 8%, runtime process restarts recorded (SIGABRT) with nvml-driver resets on a subset of dedicated runtimes. Prefetch-service reported KV-prefetch lock contention and eviction churn (kvcache.evictions/sec up 350%).
comments: 2026-03-12 10:25 - Priya Rao (Support): Customer Finlytics reported ~20% of requests returning 502/503 starting at 10:18 PDT. Provided request IDs and traces. Asked SRE to triage; escalated to P1.

2026-03-12 10:40 - Evan Chen (SRE): Initial hypothesis: accept-queue pileup from a mixed long-prompt + bulk embedding workload caused apigw backpressure, amplifying kvcache eviction thrash which in turn pushed runtimes into OOM/restart. Pulling runtime logs and NVML driver logs now.

2026-03-12 11:05 - Finlytics Support Contact (Maya Singh): Confirming workload was two large jobs started at 10:15 PDT. Provided sample payloads and tenant id. Asked if we can route to dedicated pool temporarily.

2026-03-12 12:12 - Evan Chen (SRE): Temporary mitigation applied: enabled per-tenant ingress throttling for Finlytics and routed their bulk-embedding route to a warm dedicated pool. Observed immediate decline in apigw accept_queue_depth and 5xx rate falling to ~1.2%.

2026-03-13 09:30 - Diego Morales (Runtime): Noted a pattern of 'tensor-pin' thread stalls under high eviction pressure leading to long syscall latencies; a subset of runtimes hit a watchdog and were restarted by orchestration agent. Collected core dumps for one runtime for analysis.
investigation_notes: Correlated apigw accept queue growth with bulk-embedding uploads from the same tenant; accept_queue_depth telemetry tracks with kvcache.evictions/sec spikes.
Runtime logs show repeated 'KVPrefetchLockTimeout' warnings concurrent with high eviction rates; after a threshold the runtime main thread blocked on IO and watchdog triggered restart.
NVML driver logs show resets on 3/12 morning but those align with runtime restarts rather than preceding them; hypothesis is restart is protective rather than root cause.

Traffic replay from supplied Finlytics payload reproduced accept queue growth in staging when combined with synthetic long-chat sessions; confirmed race between prefetch worker and accept/handoff path.

We observed degraded keepalive reuse (socket churn) from apigw when accept queue exceeds 5k, amplifying connection reset/retry behavior and causing hedged retries to spin up additional load on runtimes.
Linked incident SUP-661234 showed a similar pattern but was primarily NVME iowait; this event appears distinct in that kvcache lock contention is the immediate amplifier.
resolution: Short term mitigation (applied 2026-03-12 12:12): 1) Per-tenant throttling for Finlytics on bulk-embedding route. 2) Route heavy embedding uploads to a dedicated warm pool to avoid cross-traffic amplification. 3) Raised apigw accept-queue soft limit and enabled faster admission control to shed load earlier.

Root-cause (ongoing verification): Prefetch worker lock contention + kvcache eviction storm under mixed long-chat + bulk-embed workloads caused runtime main-thread stalls and watchdog restarts; accept-queue pileup at api-gateway amplified retry storms leading to elevated 5xx.

Permanent fixes planned: 1) Patch runtime to add non-blocking prefetch fallback and reduce aggressive kvcache eviction policy when accept-queue signals backpressure. 2) Add tenant-level early-shed admission at api-gateway for heavy batch routes. 3) Improve observability: surface kvcache.lock-time and accept-queue correlations in Console dashboards and add automated detector alerting. 4) Backfill tests in load harness to include mixed workloads (long chat + bulk embeds).
Follow-ups: Create task for Runtime team to implement fallback (INT-3307-runtime-prefetch-fallback). Schedule postmortem and customer debrief with Finlytics (target 2026-03-18).
